summary: Washington County, ME enclosed wooden tower built 1934 on Downeast Lakes Land Trust land; judged non-salvageable in 2025, now gone, with a July 2026 cleanup planned for a picnic site.

facts.design: enclosed wooden fire tower; the land trust's news release, reproduced in the chapter's 2025 report, calls it the last remaining enclosed wooden fire tower in New England
facts.status_note: Judged non-salvageable in 2025; the chapter report (data to 12/31/2025) said removal had not happened; a later land trust trail page calls the site former (now gone); exact removal date not found
facts.agency: Maine Forest Service managed the tower; site on Downeast Lakes Land Trust property

access.note: Former site is beside the land trust's Tower Hill Trail, which it lists among its hikes; a public picnic site was planned, not confirmed as built

visit.drive_up: Park at the West Grand Lake Dam lot or along the extension of Tower Road
visit.trail_note: Tower Hill Trail runs near the former tower site; the tower itself is gone

events.note: Built in 1934 per the chapter's 2025 report and the land trust
Structural architects and Maine Cabin Masters contractors assessed the tower and found it non-salvageable; reported in the chapter's 2025 annual report (assessment date not given)
Exact removal date not found. The chapter report (data to 12/31/2025) says removal had not occurred; a later land trust page calls the site former (now gone)
Land trust scheduled a volunteer cleanup of the former site for 07/10/2026 to turn it into a public picnic site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The land trust's trail is named Tower Hill Trail; the chapter's statewide list calls the hill Indian Hill. The story gives both names.

The chapter's report, with data as of 12/31/2025, says removal had not yet occurred. The land trust's later trail page calls the site former (now gone), and a 07/10/2026 cleanup event refers to the former tower. Removal is dated to 2026 by inference; no source read gives the exact date.

notes_for_editor: Brief said status gone and access unknown; the land trust and FFLA sources support gone, and access is now set to public from the land trust's trail listing. Removal date is inferred as 2026; the exact date and whether the 07/10/2026 cleanup took place are not in any source read. No staffing or fire history found in the sources read, so none is written. Name conflict Tower Hill (land trust) vs Indian Hill (FFLA) is left in the story. A 2023 Maine by Foot guide and a Maine Trail Finder page appeared in search results only and were not used.
